dialogues.patient_says: I keep replaying a conversation I had yesterday. Did I say something wrong? I think I did. What if they hate me now?

choices.text: I'm sure they don't hate you. You're just overthinking it.
That sounds exhausting. How long have you been thinking about this?
What specifically are you worried you said wrong?
Everyone overthinks sometimes. It will pass.

dialogues.patient_says: I made a small mistake at work and now I can't stop thinking everyone noticed. They probably think I'm incompetent.

choices.text: One mistake doesn't define your competence.
What was the mistake? Walk me through it.
Do you have any evidence they noticed or is this a feeling?
You should be more careful next time.

dialogues.patient_says: I spent three hours last night drafting one email. I kept rewriting it because it never felt right.

choices.text: Three hours on one email does sound really draining.
What were you afraid the email would come across as?
Did you ever send it?
Maybe just send it without overthinking.

dialogues.patient_says: Sometimes I wonder if people only tolerate me. Like they don't actually want me around but they're too polite to say it.

choices.text: That sounds really lonely to carry around.
Has anyone ever given you a reason to feel that way?
I'm sure your friends genuinely care about you.
Why would they tolerate you if they didn't want you around?

dialogues.patient_says: I cancelled plans with a friend because I was scared I'd say something awkward and ruin everything.

choices.text: What were you afraid you would say?
Avoiding situations can make the fear bigger over time.
That's okay, everyone needs alone time sometimes.
Your friend probably didn't even notice.

dialogues.patient_says: Do you ever feel like your brain just won't stop? Mine never does. Even when I try to sleep.

choices.text: A racing mind at night is really common with overthinking. Does it happen often?
What kinds of thoughts keep you up?
Have you tried breathing exercises before bed?
You just need to learn to relax.

dialogues.patient_says: I rehearsed what I was going to say in this session the whole way here. I was scared I'd say something wrong.

choices.text: That actually takes courage to admit. There's nothing wrong you could say here.
What were you worried about saying?
You don't need to prepare for this. Just talk.
You really don't need to overthink coming here.

dialogues.patient_says: I read a message from my friend three times and I still can't figure out if they're mad at me.

choices.text: What does the message say?
Have you considered just asking them directly?
If they were mad they would tell you.
Sometimes a message is just a message.

dialogues.patient_says: I feel stupid for worrying about things that probably don't matter. But I can't stop.

choices.text: You're not stupid. Your brain is working overtime and that's exhausting.
What makes you think they don't matter?
Worrying is just part of how your mind works.
You're right, some things aren't worth worrying about.

dialogues.patient_says: I spent all morning thinking about whether I should change my order at a coffee shop. I ended up leaving without getting anything.

choices.text: That sounds frustrating. Do small decisions often feel that difficult?
Decision fatigue is real. It happens when the brain is already overloaded.
Just pick something next time, it doesn't have to be perfect.
It's just coffee, you're making it bigger than it is.

dialogues.patient_says: I keep imagining worst case scenarios for things that haven't even happened yet.

choices.text: That's called catastrophizing. Can you give me an example?
What's the worst case scenario you keep coming back to?
Try to focus on what's actually happening right now.
The worst case rarely actually happens.

dialogues.patient_says: I apologize a lot even when I haven't done anything wrong. I just feel like I'm always in the way.

choices.text: You're not in the way here. Why do you feel like you are?
Over-apologizing often comes from anxiety. Do you notice when you do it?
Try to stop apologizing so much.
A lot of people feel that way sometimes.

dialogues.patient_says: I don't know why but I keep checking if I locked the door even after I already checked twice.

choices.text: That kind of checking behavior often comes from distrust of your own memory. Does it feel like relief when you check?
How many times do you usually end up checking?
Just trust yourself. You locked it.
Maybe put a sticky note on the door to remind yourself.

dialogues.patient_says: I had a good day yesterday but then spent the whole evening waiting for something bad to happen to cancel it out.

choices.text: That sounds like you struggle to let good things just be good.
Did something bad happen, or did the good day stay good?
You deserve good days. They don't need to be balanced.
That's a bit of a pessimistic way to live.

dialogues.patient_says: Sometimes I feel like I'm watching myself from outside my body and judging everything I do.

choices.text: That detached feeling can be really disorienting. How long does it usually last?
What does the voice say when it judges you?
Try to be kinder to yourself.
Everyone is their own harshest critic.

dialogues.patient_says: I keep making lists to feel in control but then I feel guilty when I don't finish them.

choices.text: Lists can be helpful but when they become pressure they do the opposite. Do your lists feel like pressure?
What happens when you don't finish one?
Maybe make shorter lists.
You don't have to finish everything on a list.

dialogues.patient_says: I've been thinking about a fight I had with my mom three years ago and wondering if I should have said something different.

choices.text: Three years is a long time to carry that. What keeps bringing it back?
Have you ever talked to her about it?
It was three years ago. Let it go.
What do you wish you had said?

dialogues.patient_says: I hate making phone calls. I rehearse what I'm going to say but then panic when someone actually picks up.

choices.text: Phone anxiety is very common. What part of it feels the most scary?
What do you worry will happen if the call doesn't go the way you rehearsed?
Just dial and see what happens.
Could you text instead when possible?

dialogues.patient_says: I feel like I need to understand everything completely before I can do anything. So I end up doing nothing.

choices.text: That's called analysis paralysis. Does it happen in a specific area of your life or everywhere?
What would happen if you started before you felt ready?
Sometimes you just have to start.
Not understanding everything is okay. What's one small thing you could do today?

dialogues.patient_says: I keep thinking about things I said five years ago that were embarrassing. Random moments just hit me out of nowhere.

choices.text: Those sudden memory flashes can feel really jarring. Do they come with a physical feeling too?
What do you do when they hit?
Nobody remembers those things as well as you do.
The past is the past. There's nothing you can do about it now.

dialogues.patient_says: I got a compliment today and spent an hour trying to figure out if they meant it or were just being polite.

choices.text: What would it mean for you if they genuinely meant it?
It sounds like it's hard to accept good things about yourself.
They probably meant it. Just say thank you next time.
What did they say?

dialogues.patient_says: I feel like I need everyone to like me. If even one person doesn't, it ruins everything.

choices.text: Where do you think that need comes from?
Not everyone will like everyone and that's genuinely okay.
Can you think of someone who doesn't like you right now?
You can't control whether people like you.

dialogues.patient_says: I overanalyze my own emotions so much that I'm not sure what I actually feel anymore.

choices.text: That's a really honest thing to say. What does it feel like right now in this moment?
When did you start feeling disconnected from your own emotions?
Try journaling. It might help you sort through things.
Sometimes feelings don't need to be analyzed, just felt.

dialogues.patient_says: I prepared for every possible outcome of a meeting and then it went completely differently and I just froze.

choices.text: Freezing when things go off script is tough. What happened after you froze?
No amount of preparation can cover every outcome. How did you feel about that?
You should practice being more flexible.
What would have helped you in that moment?

dialogues.patient_says: I talked to someone new today. I thought it went okay but now I'm not sure. What if I came across weird?

choices.text: What made you feel like it went okay at the time?
Hold onto that first feeling. Your gut reaction is usually more accurate.
If they thought you were weird they wouldn't have kept talking to you.
You probably did come across fine. Stop worrying.

dialogues.patient_says: My mind goes blank when someone asks me a question I didn't prepare for and then I panic.

choices.text: That blank feeling is your nervous system going into overdrive. Does it happen in specific situations?
It's okay to say you need a moment to think before answering.
You just need more confidence.
What kind of questions tend to blank you out?

dialogues.patient_says: I stayed up until 2am thinking about whether I should quit my job. I didn't come to any conclusion.

choices.text: Big decisions are hard. What's making you consider quitting?
Late night thinking rarely leads to good conclusions. How are you feeling today?
You probably shouldn't make big decisions at 2am.
What would help you feel clearer about this decision?

dialogues.patient_says: I feel guilty when I'm not being productive. Even resting feels like I'm doing something wrong.

choices.text: Rest is not the opposite of productivity. They work together. Where do you think that guilt comes from?
What does a restful moment look like for you when you allow yourself one?
You need rest. It's not optional.
Maybe try to be more productive so resting doesn't feel wasteful.

dialogues.patient_says: I asked a question in class today and immediately regretted it. I kept thinking everyone thought it was stupid.

choices.text: Asking questions takes courage. What made you regret it?
Was there any actual reaction from people or is this what you imagined?
No question is stupid.
I'm glad you asked the question. That's growth.

dialogues.patient_says: I wrote and deleted the same text message about twenty times. I still haven't sent it.

choices.text: What are you trying to say in the message?
What's the worst that happens if you send it?
Just send it. Done is better than perfect.
What would you say if you weren't afraid of the response?

dialogues.patient_says: I think about dying sometimes but not because I want to. More like I wonder what it would be like if I just wasn't here.

choices.text: Thank you for trusting me with that. Can you tell me more about when those thoughts come?
That kind of thought is worth taking seriously. Do you feel safe right now?
A lot of people feel that way sometimes.
You should talk to someone about that.

dialogues.patient_says: I convinced myself that my headache was something serious and spent two hours reading about symptoms online.

choices.text: Health anxiety is really common. Did reading about it make you feel better or worse?
The internet is not a doctor. What would help you step away from that spiral?
Stop googling symptoms. It always makes things worse.
How does your head feel now?

dialogues.patient_says: I feel bad about things I did in primary school. Like genuinely ashamed.

choices.text: Primary school is a long time ago. What keeps bringing those memories up?
The fact that you feel ashamed now says something good about who you've become.
Everyone does embarrassing things as a kid. It's normal.
What happened?

dialogues.patient_says: I find it hard to enjoy anything because I'm always thinking about what I should be doing instead.

choices.text: That constant pull between being present and being productive sounds exhausting.
When was the last time you genuinely enjoyed something without guilt?
Just allow yourself to enjoy things.
What's something you used to enjoy before this started?

dialogues.patient_says: I always feel like I need to explain myself fully or people will misunderstand me.

choices.text: Do you feel like people have misunderstood you a lot in the past?
Some misunderstanding is unavoidable. What would happen if someone misread you?
You don't owe everyone a full explanation.
Just say what you mean and move on.

dialogues.patient_says: I think I'm getting better at noticing when I start to spiral. But stopping it is still really hard.

choices.text: Noticing it is genuinely the hardest part. That's real progress.
What does the spiral feel like when it starts?
What have you tried to stop it?
If you can notice it you should be able to stop it.

dialogues.patient_says: I keep waiting to feel ready for things but the ready feeling never comes.

choices.text: Readiness often comes after starting, not before. What's something you've been waiting to feel ready for?
What does ready feel like to you?
Just start and figure it out as you go.
You might never feel fully ready and that's actually okay.

dialogues.patient_says: I feel calmer today. I'm not sure why but I wanted to mention it.

choices.text: That's worth noticing. What's been different today?
I'm really glad to hear that.
Don't get too used to it. The thoughts might come back.
See, you just needed to relax.

dialogues.patient_says: I think coming here helps. Even just having somewhere to say this stuff out loud.

choices.text: I'm glad this feels like a safe space. That matters.
What feels different about saying it out loud versus keeping it in your head?
That's what I'm here for.
You should also try talking to people in your life about this.

dialogues.patient_says: I know I think too much. I just don't know how to stop. Is that something that can actually get better?

choices.text: Yes. It takes time and practice but it genuinely does get better.
The goal isn't to stop thinking. It's to have a better relationship with your thoughts.
It depends on how much effort you put in.
Some people just think more than others.
